data:
Signal processing in pure Go (CGO_ENABLED=0): filter design and filtering, spectral estimation, resampling and peak finding, with the semantics of SciPy’s scipy.signal and, where it differs, a note on MATLAB’s.
import "github.com/go-dsp/signal" z, _ := signal.Butter(8, []float64{0.2}, signal.Lowpass, nil) // zeros, poles, gain sos, _ := z.SOS(false) // second-order sections y, _ := signal.SOSFiltFilt(sos, x, nil) // zero-phase filtering f, p, _ := signal.Welch(x, &signal.SpectralOptions{Fs: 1000, Nperseg: 1024}) The module is github.com/go-dsp/signal, BSD-3-Clause. It depends on go-fft/fft (transforms and the classic windows), go-numerics/special (complete elliptic integrals, I0) and go-simd/floats (the assembly dot product used by the FIR kernels).
remez.go’s exchange follows the Parks–McClellan program of J. H. McClellan, T. W. Parks and L. R. Rabiner (IEEE Trans. Audio Electroacoust., 1973) as SciPy’s _sigtoolsmodule.cc carries it in E. Kvaleberg’s C translation (SciPy License, BSD-3-Clause; Copyright 2005 Travis Oliphant and the SciPy developers); its control flow and label numbers are kept so the two read side by side.
data.conventions#Conventions: Signals and coefficients are []float64; filters have real coefficients and signals are real and one-dimensional (no axis argument: loop over the channels of a matrix). A filter is a ZPK (zeros, poles, gain), a transfer function (b, a) or an SOS (second-order sections). Use SOS above order 8: the transfer function form loses accuracy fast (see docs/verification.md). Functions that can fail return an error; nothing panics on bad arguments (the fuzz targets enforce it), and sizes are bounded (2^28 elements) so absurd arguments fail instead of exhausting memory. Option structs have useful zero values: nil means SciPy’s defaults. Where SciPy’s default differs between functions (detrend, scaling) the zero value is “the default of this function”.
data.layout#Layout: file contents convert.go, poly.go representations, conversions, polynomial roots freq.go frequency responses, group delay analog.go, transform.go, iir.go prototypes, band transforms, IIR design and order selection fir.go, remez.go, windows.go, linalg.go FIR design, Parks–McClellan, windows and DPSS, small solvers filter.go, convolve.go filtering, convolution spectral.go, resample.go spectral estimation, resampling, peaks *_test.go, testdata/oracle tests, SciPy oracle harness and recorded responses
data.performance#Performance: docs/perf.md: one core against SciPy on the same host, in interleaved rounds, with the load average checked (-perf -perfcase measures a subset without rewriting the table). The FIR kernels call the SIMD dot product of go-simd/floats; the recursions are serial by nature, so SOSFilt runs four (or two) sections sample-major to overlap their dependency chains and the FIR form of LFilter is a direct chain eight outputs wide, both bit-identical to the one-section, one-output form. Remez runs the McClellan–Parks–Rabiner exchange (its search walks the error curve from each extremum instead of evaluating the whole grid every iteration), PeakProminences finds every base in two monotonic-stack passes (O(n), where the per-peak scan SciPy uses is O(n·peaks)), and Spectrogram computes its PSD through one reused spectrum buffer.
data.verification#Verification:
SciPy 1.18.1 with NumPy 2.5.4 is the oracle, driven from Go (oracle_test.go: one persistent Python process, base64 float64/complex128 over JSON lines, so no decimal round trip loses a bit). Every comparison is recorded in testdata/oracle and replayed from there, so go test needs no Python and the same recorded SciPy output is checked on every architecture CI runs. GOWORK=off go test -update ./... re-records it and rewrites docs/accuracy.md, the table of maximum ULP errors, normwise relative errors and exact-equality counts for 225 groups of values; docs/verification.md explains the measures and the few places where SciPy itself is the less accurate side (ill-conditioned elliptic and Bessel designs, high-order transfer functions).
100% statement coverage with -race, including the error paths. gofmt, go vet, govulncheck; amd64, arm64, 386 (and under qemu riscv64, loong64, ppc64le, s390x, arm) and every GOOS/GOARCH pair compiling the tests. Fuzz targets for the design constructors, the spectral estimators, the convolutions and the peak finder.

knowing:
STFT/ISTFT follow SciPy’s legacy stft/istft (the ShortTimeFFT class is not provided). SciPy emits warnings where Go returns values: a singular group delay is set to zero silently; Remez returns the best filter together with ErrNotConverged (SciPy raises; a degenerate design whose taps would not be finite returns nil). EllipAP returns an error (SciPy returns NaN poles) when the stopband attenuation is below the passband ripple. Bessel prototypes use exact integer polynomial coefficients refined in 320-bit arithmetic (double precision loses the zeros above order 8) and are limited to order 150, where the delay gain overflows float64. The PadModeReflect, PadModeAntireflect, PadModeSmooth and PadModeLine extensions of a one-sample signal are undefined in SciPy; here they repeat the sample. Not provided: N-dimensional and axis variants, complex-coefficient filters, dlti/lti classes, ShortTimeFFT, savgol_filter, czt, continuous wavelets and find_peaks_cwt (wavelets are planned in this organisation).

How the package is checked against the reference tools of the domain, what the numbers in accuracy.md mean, and where the reference itself is the less accurate side.
data.corner-cases#Corner cases: The comparisons include the degenerate inputs, not only random ones: filters with a[0] != 1, with fewer zeros than poles, FIR filters through the IIR path, unit-circle poles (singular group delay), one-sample and one-segment signals, odd and even lengths everywhere, every window and every pad mode, filters longer than the signal, up larger than the filter length, plateaus in find_peaks, empty inputs, and every error path (checked to be an error in Go, and, where SciPy raises too, to be an error there).
data.fuzzing-and-limits#Fuzzing and limits: limits_test.go holds the fuzz targets (FuzzFirwin, FuzzIIRFilter, FuzzWelchOptions, FuzzFindPeaks, FuzzConvolve) and a table of absurd arguments (orders of 2^30, billions of taps, huge FFT lengths and resampling factors) that must produce an error, not a panic or an allocation. Output sizes are bounded at 2^28 elements, analog prototype orders at 65536 (Bessel at 150), firls at 16384 taps (dense normal equations).
data.gates#Gates: gofmt, go vet, go test -race with 100% statement coverage (-coverpkg=./...), GOARCH=386 (run in a 32-bit container locally, natively in CI), govulncheck, and the go test -c of every GOOS/GOARCH pair in CI.
data.measures#Measures:
For each group of values accuracy.md gives
values: how many numbers were compared; exact: how many are bit-identical to SciPy’s (measured on the recording host, arm64, where Go fuses multiply-adds and NumPy’s compiled loops do not); max ULP: the largest elementwise distance in units in the last place over the values that differ. It is meaningless near zero (a coefficient of 1e-17 that differs in its last digit is millions of ULPs) and is shown for completeness; norm err: max|got - want| / max|want| per case, maximised over the cases of the group. This is the right measure for polynomial coefficients, spectra and responses, and the one the tests assert (tolerances between 0 and 1e-5, stated next to each comparison). Roots and poles are compared as sets (greedy nearest matching) where SciPy’s order comes from LAPACK’s eigenvalue solver, and elementwise where the order is fixed by the algorithm (prototypes, band transforms, zpk2sos, iirfilter). Where SciPy’s own order depends on signed zeros (the square root of a negative real number with an imaginary part of -0.0 is -i*s, not +i*s) the Go code reproduces the sign of the zero so that the conjugate pairs come out in the same order.
data.octave-and-matlab-semantics#Octave and M:
Octave 9.2 with its signal package (GPL: used as an oracle only, run and never read or ported) checks that the MATLAB names mean what the README says (octave_test.go, responses in testdata/octave, replayed like the SciPy ones). One-time setup of the image, with Docker:
docker run --platform linux/amd64 --name octsig gnuoctave/octave:9.2.0 \ octave-cli --eval "pkg install -forge control signal" docker commit octsig go-dsp-octave-signal:9.2 GOWORK=off go test -run TestOctave -octave -count=1 . Normwise differences from Octave (Go versus Octave): butter (low, high, band, stop), cheby1, cheby2 2e-16 to 9e-16; buttord, cheb1ord, ellipord, kaiserord, findpeaks exact; firls 2e-15; remez 5e-16 (the same optimum); filter, conv, freqz, hilbert, detrend, hamming, blackman, kaiser 1e-16 to 1e-15; chebwin 2.5e-15. Three functions differ by more than rounding, and the difference is Octave’s, not a semantic one: ellip (1e-5; Octave’s design is less exact, SciPy’s and this package’s agree), and fir1/fir2 (3e-4 to 5e-3 from the window method of SciPy, which this package follows). Octave’s resample, pwelch and periodogram use other conventions (different anti-aliasing filter, one-sided scaling) and are not compared.
data.the-oracle#The oracle:
SciPy 1.18.1 with NumPy 2.5.4 (uv run --with scipy==1.18.1 --with numpy==2.5.4 python -c ...). The Python side is a 40-line generic dispatcher (no eval): it resolves a dotted name inside scipy/numpy, decodes the arguments, calls the function and encodes the result. It runs as one persistent process, speaks JSON lines over a pipe and exits on end of input. Arrays travel as base64 little-endian float64, int64 or complex128, so no decimal round trip loses a bit. The Go side is oracle_test.go; every other tool (comparisons, accuracy tables, the performance harness) is Go.
Every request/response pair is recorded in testdata/oracle/.json.gz, keyed by the position of the call within its test. go test replays them, so CI needs no Python and the same recorded SciPy output is checked on amd64, arm64, 386, arm, riscv64, loong64, ppc64le and s390x. (Keying by position, not by the bits of the arguments, matters: test signals are built with math.Sin and similar, which round differently on architectures that fuse multiply-adds.) GOWORK=off go test -update ./... re-records everything and rewrites accuracy.md.
data.where-scipy-is-the-less-accurate-side#Wh: The zeros of Bessel polynomials are notoriously ill-conditioned. SciPy computes them with kve and polishes in double precision; this package refines them with Newton’s method in 320-bit arithmetic on the exact integer coefficients (besselap). Against a 60-digit mpmath solution SciPy’s poles are accurate to 1e-15; in double precision alone the same recurrence loses 1e-8 by order 17, which is why the refinement exists. The two agree to 1e-12 up to order 25.
data.where-the-numbers-are-not-1e-16#Where th: group norm err why elliptic prototypes (ellipap k) 1.7e-8 Pole positions are ill-conditioned in the stopband attenuation and the order. The tests compare up to order 16. At order 18-30 SciPy itself misses the requested passband ripple by 1e-7 to 6e-3 (checked by evaluating the squared magnitude at the passband edge for both implementations), and so does this package, differently. order selection wn (buttord, cheb1ord, cheb2ord, ellipord) and iirdesign 1e-7 Band-stop edges come from a bounded scalar search with xtol = 1e-5 (fminbound); a one-ULP difference in the objective moves the optimum by far more than 1 ULP. besselap norm mag 1e-13 SciPy finds the -3 dB point with a secant search that stops at 1.5e-8; this package uses the same search. iirfilter transfer functions at order 16-40 (high ba num) 1.2e-8 The monomial form of a high-order filter is ill-conditioned: coefficient errors of 1e-8 are in the problem, not in either implementation. Compared in zpk (4e-16) and sos (4e-16) form the two agree to rounding. This is why the package recommends SOS. tf2sos, zpk2tf 1.6e-14 Same cause, at moderate order. dpss windows 1.5e-13 Eigenvectors of the tridiagonal problem by bisection and inverse iteration; LAPACK’s stebz/stein differ in rounding. chebwin 2.6e-13 The window is the inverse FFT of a Chebyshev polynomial sampled near its zeros. remez 4.8e-14 Parks-McClellan converges to the optimum of the discrete problem, and the grid is built as SciPy builds it. filtfilt with method="gust" 4.7e-15 Least squares by Householder QR instead of LAPACK’s SVD driver.
